prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across frames 1 to 3, the depth map captures the open flatbed of a small pickup truck directly in front of and below the camera wearer, packed with stacked 20-litre plastic water jugs and a metal hand trolley on top (in frame 1), where the nearest jugs at the lower-left and lower-centre are brightest at roughly 0.4–1.0 m (within the camera wearer's arm's reach) and recede across the bed to about 2.0–2.5 m near the cab. As the camera wearer turns left and moves toward the front of the truck in frames 4 and 5, the truck cab (1.2–2.5 m away on the right) and a man wearing a green face mask and blue shirt come into view on the left; he stands about 1.8–2.2 m away in frame 4 facing and looking toward the camera wearer (within arm's reach of the truck cab and nearby jugs), then approaches to roughly 0.8–1.0 m at the lower-centre in frame 5 with his head tilted down and torso cut off by the bottom frame edge. In the background of frames 4 and 5, a wheeled concrete hopper sits about 5–7 m away to the left of the truck, while distant construction workers (roughly 12–15 m away) and multi-storey buildings under construction (50+ m away) fade into near-black darkness. The depth map clearly separates the 3D layering of the overlapping, similarly coloured translucent jugs and the foreground-to-background distance jumps that are visually ambiguous in the RGB image. However, it is unreliable on the translucent plastic jugs where internal refraction flattens surface relief, through the truck's rear window which is filled in as a solid surface at the cab's depth, and at far ranges beyond 15 m where buildings, cranes, and sky clip to uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates individual foreground water jugs in frames 1 to 3 (0.5–2.0 m in front of the camera wearer), the truck cab on the right in frames 4 and 5 (1.2–2.5 m away), and the masked man on the left who moves from roughly 2.0 m in frame 4 to under 1.0 m at the bottom-centre in frame 5. It also detects tiny distant figures and vehicles that are hard to spot at a glance in the RGB strip, including a person and motorcycle parked ~15–20 m away at the upper-left of frame 1, two distant people ~20–25 m away at the upper-right of frame 3, and two helmeted workers ~12–15 m away between the foreground man and the truck cab in frame 4. In frame 5, the close-up man at the bottom-centre is split into two adjacent 'person' masks (a brown mask on his head and a blue mask on his right shoulder), while the truck mask in frame 4 is heavily occluded on the lower right by the unlabelled foreground water jugs protruding from the bed. While the map helps separate overlapping cylindrical containers and distant background pedestrians from clutter, its class labels and recall are highly unreliable for industrial objects. Specifically, the 20-litre water jugs are misclassified as 'vase', 'bottle', or 'cup' while the majority of the stacked jugs, the metal hand trolley in frame 1, the truck bed in frames 1–3, and the construction hopper and cranes in frames 4–5 are missed entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, and contains only a small, partial yellow body skeleton in the lower-right quadrant of frame 4. That single detection sits near the bottom-left corner of the truck cab (roughly 1.5–2.0 m in front of the camera wearer) with a few clustered upper-body keypoints, a diagonal limb segment, and an isolated lower keypoint, and no magenta hand skeletons appear in any frame. In the RGB strip, the camera wearer's own hands are out of view (except a tiny sliver of skin at the bottom edge of frame 1), distant pedestrians in frames 1 and 3 are 15–25 m away, and the main foreground person stands at 1.8–2.2 m on the left in frame 4 facing the camera wearer before moving to ~0.8–1.0 m at the bottom-centre in frame 5 with his torso cropped out by the lower frame boundary. Compared to the RGB image alone, the pose map adds virtually no usable spatial information and instead highlights severe detector failure under occlusion and cropping. It is unreliable throughout: it completely misses the clearly visible foreground man standing on the left in frame 4, the close-up head and shoulders of the same man in frame 5, and the distant construction workers, while placing a misplaced phantom skeleton onto the side of the truck and water jugs in frame 4.
